items.description: An authored screen material: how a display's face draws its picture through the screen shading's display treatment, a row of the document's screenMaterials that screens and creation faces name by Id. The treatment models a display's own pixel structure over the picture, which always fills the face: a darkening between source rows, coloured stripes across each source column, a radial vignette, a glint at grazing angles, and the face's rounded, softened edge. Every term is the author's (the standard package authors a cathode-ray tube, worlds/standard/skin.puck); zero turns a term off, and a view's screen fidelity fades the whole treatment out as a seat frames the screen. Presentation only: a material never moves the mapping a pointer hit takes.

id.description: The id screens and faces name the material by; unique among the document's materials.

scanlines.description: How dark the gap between source rows draws, in [0, 1]: one source row a cosine period.

subpixelStripes.description: How strong the red, green and blue stripes across each source column draw, in [0, 1].

vignette.description: How much the face darkens toward its corners, in [0, 1].

glint.description: How bright the glass's rim glint at grazing view angles adds, in [0, 1].

glintPower.description: How tightly the glint hugs grazing angles: the exponent of one minus the view cosine, positive.

cornerRadius.description: The face's corner rounding, as a fraction of the face, in [0, 0.5).

edgeSoftness.description: The width over which the face's edge fades to black, as a fraction of the face, in [0, 0.5).
